tools.title: Fraction Cubes: Volume of Prisms
tools.intro: Pack a box whose edges are fractions with small cubes of edge 1, 1/2 or 1/4. Count the cubes, find the volume of one, and see that V = lwh still works.
tools.description: Set the length, width and height in halves from 1/2 to 4 units and pack the prism with cubes of edge 1, 1/2 or 1/4. The drawing shows every small cube on the visible faces, and the readout counts the cubes along each edge, multiplies by the volume of one cube and compares the result with l × w × h. Fractions and divisions are shown stacked.
tools.discovery: Along an edge of length l there are l ÷ e cubes of edge e. The number of cubes times the volume of one cube equals l × w × h, so V = lwh works for fractional edges. Eight cubes of edge 1/2 make one unit cube.

tools.title: Nets and Surface Area
tools.intro: See a box and its net side by side, with matching colors for each pair of faces. Add the face areas to find the surface area, and compare closed and open boxes.
tools.description: Choose whole-number length, width and height. The net (six rectangles in a cross) and an oblique drawing of the box use the same color for each pair of matching faces: top and bottom, front and back, left and right. The readout adds the pairs for the surface area and gives the volume; an open-box option leaves out the top.
tools.discovery: A rectangular prism has three pairs of matching faces, so SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. An open box uses one l by w face less. Boxes with the same volume can have different surface areas.
